raw_review_excerpt:
The plan is well-grounded against the actual codebase. graphifyBuild() at graphify.cjs:461 already does the build preflight the plan says not to duplicate. The CLI router at gsd-tools.cjs:1009 supports adding context-status as a single new branch. All existing graphify functions are config-gated; the plan's explicit decision to ungate the new checker is internally justified and consistent. .planning/graphs/ root authority matches code reality across query/status/diff. No correctness or feasibility blockers found. Four issues remain: state-precedence ordering for overlapping conditions, no concrete repo-size threshold, missing CLI help-string update, and a test-placement ambiguity for the "both roots exist" case.

Issues:
- 1. [WARN] State precedence undefined for overlapping conditions
- 2. [NOTE] No concrete repo-size threshold for recommended vs not_needed
- 3. [NOTE] CLI help string at gsd-tools.cjs:1029 needs context-status
- 4. [NOTE] Test for both-roots-exist targets wrong surface

issues.title: State precedence undefined for overlapping conditions
issues.details: Seven checker states are enumerated but their priority ordering is unspecified. Multiple conditions can be true simultaneously (e.g. graphify-out/ exists + .graphifyignore missing + repo is large). Without a precedence rule, implementation will require design decisions the plan doesn't capture, and tests can't pin expected behavior for compound cases.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a precedence table or decision flowchart: check conditions in a defined order and return the first matching state. For example: unavailable > unsafe_missing_ignore > available > available_standard_only > stale > recommended > not_needed.

issues.title: No concrete repo-size threshold for recommended vs not_needed
issues.details: The plan says 'use a conservative heuristic such as tracked file count or relevant docs/code count' but commits to no number. Tests listed in Phase 4 don't include threshold-boundary cases, so the test matrix can't fully cover the heuristic without an implementation-time design decision.
issues.suggested_fix: Either commit to a threshold in the plan (e.g. >200 tracked files = recommended) or explicitly note that the threshold is a design decision deferred to implementation with a follow-up test pass.

issues.title: CLI help string at gsd-tools.cjs:1029 needs context-status
issues.details: The existing fallthrough error message lists 'Available: build, query, status, diff'. Adding context-status requires updating this string. The plan's implementation section doesn't enumerate this touchpoint.
issues.suggested_fix: Add 'update gsd-tools.cjs graphify subcommand error message to include context-status' to the Phase 2 implementation checklist.

issues.title: Test for both-roots-exist targets wrong surface
issues.details: The Phase 4 test 'both roots exist and .planning/graphs/ remains the GSD query/diff root' describes behavior of graphifyQuery/graphifyDiff, not of graphifyContextStatus. The new checker should report both roots and their states; the root-authority assertion belongs on the existing query/diff functions which are not being changed.
issues.suggested_fix: Reframe the test: 'both roots exist → checker reports available (not available_standard_only) because .planning/graphs/ mirror is present'. Drop the query/diff root-authority assertion from the checker test — that's already covered by existing graphifyQuery/graphifyDiff tests.

evidence_sources: get-shit-done/bin/gsd-tools.cjs (lines 1-1060, CLI router and graphify case)
commands/gsd/graphify.md (lines 1-80, command doc header and config gate)
review.best_case: The plan produces a clean, minimal read-only checker that lets GSD detect graph availability across both artifact roots without touching any existing behavior. The ungated design lets GSD recommend Graphify before config is set — filling the current gap where users have no way to discover whether Graphify would help. Implementation is a single new function plus one CLI branch, with clear test coverage. All existing graphify functions remain unchanged.
strongest_objections: State precedence is undefined: with seven possible states and overlapping trigger conditions, implementation will require design decisions the plan doesn't capture. This isn't a blocker but will slow implementation and make test assertions ambiguous.
The repo-size heuristic for recommended vs not_needed has no concrete threshold. Without a number, the test matrix is incomplete and the behavior is effectively undefined until implementation time.
The plan doesn't enumerate the gsd-tools.cjs help-string touchpoint for the new context-status subcommand — a minor but real gap in the implementation checklist.
hidden_assumptions: The plan assumes graphify-out/ will always be at cwd/graphify-out — but Graphify's output directory may be configurable in some setups. No plan to detect a non-default output path.

The plan assumes fs.existsSync checks on artifact files are sufficient for freshness — but doesn't define what 'stale by age threshold' means concretely (24h? configurable?). The existing graphifyStatus uses 24h hardcoded, but the checker may want a different or configurable threshold.
The plan assumes GSD_GRAPHIFY_REQUIRE_SOURCE will be an env var, but the open question about config key vs env var is unresolved. Implementation will need to pick one.

The plan assumes the checker needs no config gate, but doesn't address whether an ungated function reading filesystem state in every project (even non-Graphify ones) has any performance or noise implications.
review.what_would_change_my_mind: If state-precedence ambiguity caused the implementation to produce inconsistent test results across the seven states, or if the ungated checker introduced measurable latency in non-Graphify projects due to filesystem probing, I would escalate the precedence and gating issues from WARN/NOTE to BLOCK. Currently neither is evidenced — the checker is pure filesystem reads (fast) and the precedence gap is a design clarity issue, not a correctness failure.
